title: fs.promises

blocks.md:
## From callbacks to promises

Old Node: `fs.readFile(path, (err, data) => …)`. The first argument is the error, or `null` when the read worked. New style: `await fs.promises.readFile(path, "utf8")` and `try/catch`.

You still read the same fixture. The promise version returns text instead of stuffing it into a callback. The source must mention `promises` so the habit is visible.

The desk used to check `err` first. Now the fox walk slip is awaited: read `note.txt`, trim, print `north`.

blocks.promptMd: In `fs.readFile(path, cb)`, the first callback argument is…
In `fs.readFile(path, cb)`, the first callback argument is the file text.
blocks.explainMd: Error first: err is argument 0. The bytes or text come second, and only if err is null.

blocks.promptMd: > `async function load()` uses `fs.promises` to read `note.txt`. Print trimmed `north`.

hintLadder.md: `load` is async. Read with `fs.promises`, not the callback form.
Await the read, then `trim()` the text.

description: Older file calls pass an error first. Newer ones return a promise.
